children: The Czech koruna is little changed after the Czech National Bank held interest rates at 3.75% as expected. "Although the latest inflation data has picked up, making rate hikes seem more urgent, recent statements by officials suggest that monetary policy is still sufficiently restrictive," Commerzbank's Tatha Ghose says in a note. The CNB's relatively restrictive stance compared to the Polish and Hungarian central banks should support the koruna in coming months, he says. The CNB raised rates by 25 basis points in June, marking its first increase since 2022. The euro trades steady at 24.301 koruna. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
